answer: At harvest the beekeeper seals every jar with his own wax and weighs the honey in the apiary book, and only a sealed jar may be sold at the fair. A pearl jar filled with bought honey breaks the seal: the ivory of the harvest must weigh what the hives gave, and a bought jar tastes of lowland clover. Faking the harvest means keeping 60 hives for a year, buying wax and paying 10,300, while the sparrow seal on each jar is cracked open by the buyer, so a jar whose harvest was never weighed is poured back into the hive.
